cases.notes: Their mark, untouched, and no second one derived. A caller writing cacheType is working in the mark-in-place idiom and budgeting against its limit of four; spending another on their behalf is how a request that worked starts failing. The create-and-reference column still caches the prefix, and that is not an inconsistency: cacheType is ONE provider's option and says nothing about what another provider should do. The first version of this row said null for both, and the runner caught it -- which is the argument for a runner over a written-down expectation.

cases.notes: The row to read first. Nothing stable precedes the volatile message, so there is no prefix to cache and the right answer is to mark NOTHING — a port that marked something here would look like it was doing more work rather than less. The warning is the only output, and it is the only half of this feature that helps a caller whose provider has no breakpoints at all.
